neighbours.label: an office, force or pupil about to be placed 'under' a leader (Secretary of State | under …, a brigade | under General …); the pole promotes ' under'
fire: John Hay was Secretary of State under Theodore Roosevelt.
She worked as press secretary under two different presidents.
A Confederate brigade under General Hood attacked the hill.
He trained as a painter under the Dutch master Rembrandt.
The fleet sailed south under Admiral Nelson's command.
Robert Rubin served as Treasury secretary under Bill Clinton.
Baghdad fell to the Mongols under Hulegu in 1258.
She served as deputy director under the agency's first chief.
quiet: John Hay wrote poetry and a biography of Lincoln.
She worked as a nurse in two different hospitals.
A Confederate cemetery sits on top of the hill.
He bought a painting by the Dutch master Rembrandt.
The fleet was repaired in the harbour at Portsmouth.
Robert Rubin wrote a memoir about his years on Wall Street.
Baghdad was famous for its libraries and its scholars.
She became director of the museum in 2004.

notes: The + pole's output suppresses ' under' / ' Under' / ' beneath', so this - pole promotes them.
